spec.title: codexlb2otel - Full Telemetry
spec.description: Every signal codexlb2otel emits: all 63 metrics, all 9 Loki record types, and the trace tree. Twelve tabs, from agent behaviour through to the exporter's own health. Generated by dashboards/v2/generate.py, which fails the build if any declared metric or record type loses its last panel.

spec.name: model
spec.label: Model
spec.description: Filters every panel whose metric carries gen_ai_request_model. Metrics without that label (the selfobs family) deliberately ignore it.

spec.name: account
spec.label: Account
spec.description: Grafana Cloud-style account id from the archive. Rate limits and credits are per account.

spec.name: kind
spec.label: Request kind
spec.description: turn, prewarm, compaction, memory. These run CONCURRENTLY on one thread - filtering to turn hides real spend.

spec.name: record_type
spec.label: Log record type
spec.description: Loki stream label. One of nine record kinds.

spec.name: family
spec.label: Transport family
spec.description: Metric family selector. All non-probe families are selected by default; probe remains available for cost analysis.

spec.name: id
spec.label: Lookup ID
spec.description: Exact request, response, or thread ID for the Lookup panel.

spec.name: search
spec.label: Log search
spec.description: Case-insensitive regex applied to log line content on the Conversation Logs tab. Leave as . to match everything.

options.content:
**Metric timestamps are INGEST time, not event time.** The exporter tails an archive and records into
the OTel SDK as it reads, so replaying a backlog - after a restart, or on first deployment - lands hours
of traffic on a few minutes of wall clock. A tall narrow spike across every panel at the same instant is
that, not a traffic surge. Cross-check against **ingest lag**: if it was high and falling at that moment,
you are looking at catch-up.

The **logs** do not have this problem (they carry the record's own timestamp, and anything older than
3h is dropped rather than backdated), and neither do the **traces**. Only the metrics.

`request_kind` - turn, prewarm, compaction, memory - are **concurrent series on one thread**, not phases
of one another. Filtering to `turn` hides real spend.

spec.title: Ingest lag
spec.description: Wall clock now minus the newest record timestamp the tailer has seen. The one number that tells you whether anything else on this dashboard is current. Healthy is roughly the poll interval (5s). This is the ONLY wall-clock subtraction anywhere in the pipeline - everything else is measured against the archive's own clock.

spec.title: Turns
spec.description: Logical turns completed in the selected range. A turn is the whole user-visible exchange; a response is one model call within it.

spec.title: Responses
spec.description: Model responses in range. Responses per turn above ~1 means the harness is looping - tool calls, retries, or continuation.

spec.title: Tokens
spec.description: input + output ONLY. Summing every gen_ai.token.type would double-count: cache_read is a sub-bucket nested inside input, and reasoning inside output, not additive siblings of them. See the Tokens tab.

spec.title: Spend in range
spec.description: Observed enriched spend in the selected range. Probe traffic is excluded by the family selector.

spec.title: Spend rate
spec.description: Observed enriched spend per second, excluding probe traffic by default.

spec.title: Errors
spec.description: Error events in range, from the archive's own error records - not this exporter's health. Zero is the expected value.

spec.title: Rate-limit headroom (worst account)
spec.description: 100 minus the highest primary-window utilisation across accounts. This is the number that decides whether the next request gets served.

spec.title: Turn and response rate
spec.description: Three levels of the same traffic: turns (user-visible), responses (model calls), engine calls (upstream inference invocations). The gaps between them are where tool loops and retries live.

spec.title: Turn duration percentiles
spec.description: End-to-end logical turn latency by model. Decomposed on the Latency tab.

spec.title: Token rate (additive: input + output)
spec.description: Only input and output are stacked, because only they are additive. cache_read and reasoning are breakdowns NESTED inside them and appear on the Tokens tab, unstacked - stacking a sub-bucket on its parent silently doubles the total.

spec.expr: sum by (gen_ai_token_type) (rate(codexlb_tokens_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family", gen_ai_token_type=~"input|output"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.title: Traffic by model
spec.description: Which model is actually doing the work.

spec.expr: sum by (gen_ai_request_model) (increase(codexlb_responses_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family", gen_ai_request_model!=""}[$__range]))

spec.title: Pipeline and sink health
spec.description: Steady values are healthy. Open responses climbing without bound means completion frames are not arriving and the reducer is accumulating.

spec.title: Log volume by record type
spec.description: Every line this exporter pushes to Loki, by kind. Backlog older than loki.max_line_age (3h) is dropped locally rather than silently discarded server-side, so a gap here during catch-up is expected, not a fault.

spec.title: Which instrument can answer which question

options.content:
Model usage over time, **grouped and ungrouped by reasoning effort**. Effort is not on every
instrument, and filtering by a label a series does not carry empties the panel silently rather than
erroring, so this tab is arranged around one fact:

**`codexlb.responses` and `codexlb.turns` carry BOTH `gen_ai.request.model` and
`gen_ai.request.reasoning.level`. No token, duration or tool-call instrument carries effort.**

So every effort-split panel here counts **requests**, never tokens. Token shape by effort is a
LogQL question and lives on the **Tokens & Cost** tab. The one token panel here is by model only,
and says so.

`responses` counts every model response, prewarm included; `turns` excludes prewarm and compaction.
Where the two disagree the gap is client-tagged prewarm - real billed traffic, not noise.

spec.title: Response rate by model
spec.description: Model usage over time, NOT split by effort. Stacked, so the top of the stack is total response rate.

spec.expr: sum by (gen_ai_request_model) (rate(codexlb_responses_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family", gen_ai_request_model!=""}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.title: Turn rate by model
spec.description: The same shape with prewarm and compaction excluded - real work only. A model whose turn rate sits far below its response rate is being prewarmed more than it is being used.

spec.expr: sum by (gen_ai_request_model) (rate(codexlb_turns_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family", gen_ai_request_model!=""}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.title: Response rate by model and reasoning effort
spec.description: The grouped view, and the reason this tab exists. It shows an effort shift WITHIN a single model, which the by-model panel above averages away - and effort moves reasoning-token spend far harder than request count does.

spec.expr: sum by (gen_ai_request_model, gen_ai_request_reasoning_level) (rate(codexlb_responses_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family", gen_ai_request_model!=""}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.title: Model mix over time (% of responses)
spec.description: The same series normalised to 100%, so a change in the mix stays readable while total volume moves. Normalisation is the panel's percent stacking, not the query - the underlying values are still rates.

spec.expr: sum by (gen_ai_request_model) (rate(codexlb_responses_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family", gen_ai_request_model!=""}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.title: Reasoning effort mix over time (%)
spec.description: Effort mix with the model collapsed. Read it against the panel to its left: the model split can hold steady while the effort mix drifts upward.

spec.title: Responses by model
spec.description: Whole-window totals per model, ungrouped.

spec.expr: sum by (gen_ai_request_model) (increase(codexlb_responses_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family", gen_ai_request_model!=""}[$__range]))

spec.title: Responses by reasoning effort
spec.description: Whole-window totals per reasoning level, across every model.

spec.expr: sum by (gen_ai_request_reasoning_level) (increase(codexlb_responses_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family"}[$__range]))

spec.title: Responses by model and effort
spec.description: The two dimensions crossed and ranked - the flat ordering behind the stacked time series above.

spec.expr: sum by (gen_ai_request_model, gen_ai_request_reasoning_level) (increase(codexlb_responses_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family", gen_ai_request_model!=""}[$__range]))

spec.title: Model x effort totals
spec.description: The numbers behind the tab, with request kind as a third column so prewarm is visible rather than folded into the model total. Sort any column.

spec.expr: sum by (gen_ai_request_model, gen_ai_request_reasoning_level, codexlb_request_kind) (increase(codexlb_responses_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family", gen_ai_request_model!=""}[$__range]))

spec.title: Response rate by reasoning effort
spec.description: Absolute effort volume over time, drawn as bars so each bucket reads as a discrete count rather than a smoothed area.

spec.title: Token rate by model
spec.description: What the model mix costs in tokens, grouped by model only. codexlb.tokens also carries reasoning effort; the Tokens & Cost tab exposes that split. Input + output only; cache_read and reasoning are sub-buckets nested inside those two and stacking them on their own parents double-counts.

spec.title: Distinct agent versions by model
spec.description: Distinct instructions-hash versions observed per model. A sudden increase means agent instructions changed or diverged.

spec.expr: count by (gen_ai_request_model) (count by (gen_ai_request_model, gen_ai_agent_version) (increase(codexlb_responses_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_family=~"$family"}[$__rate_interval]) > 0))

spec.title: Responses by status
spec.description: completed is the happy path. Anything else is worth a look on the Errors tab.

spec.title: Responses by request kind
spec.description: turn, prewarm, compaction and memory run CONCURRENTLY on the same thread - they are separate metric series, not phases of one another. Prewarm and compaction volume is invisible to the user but not to the bill.

spec.title: Turns by originator and thread source
spec.description: Which client produced the traffic and how the thread began.

spec.expr: sum by (codexlb_originator, codexlb_thread_source) (increase(codexlb_turns_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family"}[$__range]))

spec.title: Response outcome matrix
spec.description: The three labels that matter, crossed. Read it as: which model, doing what, ended how.

spec.expr: sum by (gen_ai_request_model, codexlb_status, codexlb_request_kind) (increase(codexlb_responses_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family"}[$__range]))

spec.title: Reasoning level and service tier
spec.description: Reasoning level drives both latency and reasoning-token spend; service tier drives queueing.

spec.expr: sum by (gen_ai_request_reasoning_level) (increase(codexlb_responses_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family"}[$__range]))

sum by (codexlb_service_tier) (increase(codexlb_responses_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family"}[$__range]))

spec.title: Request vs response model (substitution)
spec.description: These differ when the service substitutes a model. A row where they do not match is not an error, but it changes what you are actually paying for and what latency to expect.

spec.expr: sum by (gen_ai_request_model, gen_ai_response_model) (increase(codexlb_responses_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family"}[$__range]))

spec.title: Proxy status versus wire status
spec.description: Per-turn proxy verdict beside the status inferred from the captured wire response. Disagreement is diagnostic, not silently collapsed.

spec.expr: {service_name="codexlb2otel", codexlb_record_type="turn"} | json proxy_status="proxy_status", proxy_error_code="proxy_error_code", wire_status="status" | proxy_status!=""

spec.title: Operation duration by request and response model
spec.description: Duration histogram samples grouped by requested and response model. Compare unlike pairs to identify safety-buffering reruns; PromQL cannot compare two label values in a matcher.

spec.title: Baseline resets
spec.description: A cumulative counter on a thread went backwards, so the reducer rebased it. Expected at thread start and after a reconnect; a sustained rate means sequence tracking is losing frames and per-response deltas may be wrong.

spec.title: Attributes rejected by the cardinality guard
spec.description: One guard per process caps distinct values per attribute. A non-zero rate means real values are being dropped to protect cardinality - the metric is still correct in aggregate but a dimension has gone lossy. Investigate before raising the cap.

spec.title: Recent turn records
spec.description: One line per completed logical turn, carrying the full structured metadata set - thread, session, window, account, plan, token usage. Expand a line to pivot into any of it.

spec.title: gen_ai.token.type is NOT a flat enum

options.content:
`input` and `output` are additive siblings. **`cache_read` is nested inside `input`** and **`reasoning`
is nested inside `output`** - they are breakdowns of their parent, not peers of it. Summing or stacking
all four double-counts, which is why the panels below keep the additive view and the nested view apart,
and why the ratio panel divides `cache_read` by `input` rather than by `input + cache_read`.

That nesting is also what `gen_ai_token_semantics="inclusive"` declares on these series, so a consumer
never has to infer it from the provider name.

The same trap is why `engine_uncached_prompt_tokens` is deliberately a separate metric rather than a
fifth `gen_ai.token.type` value: `uncached = input - cache_read` is another nested breakdown, and putting
it on the same axis would double-count against `input` for anyone who did not know to exclude it.

spec.title: Additive token volume (input + output)
spec.description: Safe to stack: these two do not overlap, so the stack height is the real total.

spec.expr: sum by (gen_ai_token_type) (rate(codexlb_tokens_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family", gen_ai_token_type=~"input|output"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.title: Nested breakdowns (cache_read within input, reasoning within output)
spec.description: Deliberately NOT stacked. Each line is a subset of one of the lines in the panel above, so stacking them together would be arithmetically meaningless.

spec.expr: sum by (gen_ai_token_type) (rate(codexlb_tokens_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family", gen_ai_token_type=~"cache_read|reasoning"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.title: Cache read ratio
spec.description: cache_read / input. The denominator is input alone, NOT input + cache_read, because cache_read is already counted inside input - dividing by the sum would understate the hit rate and can never reach 100%. This is the single biggest lever on spend, and it collapses whenever the prompt prefix changes: a system-prompt edit shows up here before it shows up on the bill.

spec.expr: 100 * sum(rate(codexlb_tokens_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family", gen_ai_token_type="cache_read"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum(rate(codexlb_tokens_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family", gen_ai_token_type="input"}[$__rate_interval])), 0.001)

spec.title: Uncached prompt tokens
spec.description: The engine's own count of prompt tokens it had to process rather than reuse. Cross-check against the cache ratio above: they should move inversely.

spec.title: Token usage distribution (gen_ai semconv)
spec.description: The OTel GenAI standard histogram, kept alongside the codexlb counter deliberately: this one is per-request DISTRIBUTION, the counter is volume. A rising p99 with flat volume is prompt growth.

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, gen_ai_token_type) (rate(gen_ai_client_token_usage_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, gen_ai_token_type) (rate(gen_ai_client_token_usage_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, gen_ai_token_type) (rate(gen_ai_client_token_usage_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

spec.title: Tokens by model and kind
spec.description: Where the tokens actually went. Sort by value to find the expensive corner - it is often compaction or prewarm rather than user turns.

spec.expr: sum by (gen_ai_request_model, codexlb_request_kind, gen_ai_token_type) (increase(codexlb_tokens_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family"}[$__range]))

spec.title: Cost by model, effort, thread source, family, and API key
spec.description: Enriched spend split across bounded cost dimensions. The default family selection excludes probes.

spec.expr: sum by (gen_ai_request_model, gen_ai_request_reasoning_level, codexlb_thread_source, codexlb_family, codexlb_api_key_name) (rate(codexlb_cost_usd_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.title: Cost split by request kind
spec.description: Compaction and memory spend are visible here even when the proxy request log does not show them.

spec.expr: sum by (codexlb_request_kind) (increase(codexlb_cost_usd_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family"}[$__range]))

spec.title: Cost per turn
spec.description: Enriched user-turn cost divided by completed logical turns. Background prewarm, compaction, and memory costs are excluded from both operands.

spec.expr: sum(increase(codexlb_cost_usd_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind="turn", codexlb_family=~"$family"}[$__range])) / clamp_min(sum(increase(codexlb_turns_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind="turn", codexlb_family=~"$family"}[$__range])), 1)

spec.title: Cost per 1M tokens by model
spec.description: Cost normalized by additive input plus output tokens; nested token buckets are excluded.

spec.expr: 1e6 * sum by (gen_ai_request_model) (increase(codexlb_cost_usd_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family"}[$__range])) / clamp_min(sum by (gen_ai_request_model) (increase(codexlb_tokens_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family", gen_ai_token_type=~"input|output"}[$__range])), 1)

spec.title: Tokens by family, effort, and thread source
spec.description: Counter-native token dimensions replace the prior LogQL workaround.

spec.expr: sum by (codexlb_family, gen_ai_request_reasoning_level, codexlb_thread_source) (rate(codexlb_tokens_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family", gen_ai_token_type=~"input|output"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.title: Image generation tokens
spec.description: NO DATA IS THE EXPECTED STATE on this capture - no image generation has occurred. The panel exists so the first image-generating turn is visible immediately rather than being invisible until someone thinks to look.

spec.title: Web search requests
spec.description: Also expected empty on this capture. Web search is billed separately from tokens, so it is worth its own panel rather than being folded into tool calls.

spec.title: Credits balance
spec.description: Remaining credit, per account. Flat at zero with unlimited=1 below is a plan without a balance, not an exhausted one.

spec.title: Unlimited plan
spec.description: 1 when the account's plan carries no credit limit. Reads the credits balance above for you - a zero balance means nothing on an unlimited plan.

spec.title: What fast mode can and cannot prove

options.content:
**Fast mode is `codexlb_service_tier_requested="priority"`.** Normal traffic is the series where
that requested-tier label is absent; it is not a request for `default`. The separately captured
`codexlb_service_tier` is what the response reports, and responses can report `default` or `auto`
even when the request asked for `priority`.

The **reported priority rate** therefore answers whether response metadata acknowledges the request.
It does not prove how the request was queued. Latency comparisons answer whether fast traffic was
observably faster, but they are observational rather than an A/B experiment. Use the per-model and
request-kind effect panels with their sample counts: an overall mean would mostly measure a changing
mix of models and work, not the effect of fast mode.

Positive improvement means fast was faster; negative means it was slower. A blank comparison means
the selected window does not contain both fast and normal samples for the same cohort.

spec.title: Fast requests
spec.description: Responses whose request explicitly asked for priority processing in the selected range.

spec.title: Fast share
spec.description: Share of selected responses that explicitly asked for priority. Normal is an absent requested-tier label, not a requested value called default.

spec.expr: 100 * (sum(increase(codexlb_responses_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family", codexlb_service_tier_requested="priority"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) / clamp_min(sum(increase(codexlb_responses_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family"}[$__range])), 1)

spec.title: Reported priority rate
spec.description: Of requests that asked for priority, the percentage whose response also reported priority. This is metadata agreement, not proof of queue treatment; default or auto may mean the request was declined or that the response does not echo the applied tier.

spec.expr: 100 * (sum(increase(codexlb_responses_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family", codexlb_service_tier_requested="priority", codexlb_service_tier="priority"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) / clamp_min(sum(increase(codexlb_responses_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family", codexlb_service_tier_requested="priority"}[$__range])), 1)

spec.title: Requested fast traffic by reported tier
spec.description: Only requests that asked for priority, split by the tier reported in each response. An empty reported value is preserved rather than rewritten.

spec.expr: sum by (codexlb_service_tier) (rate(codexlb_responses_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family", codexlb_service_tier_requested="priority"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.title: TTFT sample sizes by cohort
spec.description: The exact denominator for the TTFT comparison. A blank requested tier is normal traffic. Do not interpret a large percentage based on a tiny cohort.

spec.expr: round(sum by (gen_ai_request_model, codexlb_request_kind, codexlb_service_tier_requested) (increase(gen_ai_client_time_to_first_token_seconds_count{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_family=~"$family", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__range])))

spec.title: Time to first token by requested mode
spec.description: Perceived responsiveness grouped by what Codex asked for. Blank is normal; priority is fast. This aggregate distribution shows shape; the cohort-normalized effect below is the fairer comparison.

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, codexlb_service_tier_requested) (rate(gen_ai_client_time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_family=~"$family", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, codexlb_service_tier_requested) (rate(gen_ai_client_time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_family=~"$family", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, codexlb_service_tier_requested) (rate(gen_ai_client_time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_family=~"$family", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

spec.title: Fast TTFT improvement by model and kind
spec.description: Mean TTFT improvement within the same model and request kind: 100 × (normal - fast) / normal. Positive is faster. Cohorts without both modes are absent, avoiding a misleading cross-model aggregate.

spec.expr: (100 * ((sum by (gen_ai_request_model, codexlb_request_kind) (increase(gen_ai_client_time_to_first_token_seconds_sum{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_family=~"$family", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_service_tier_requested!~"priority"}[$__range])) / clamp_min(sum by (gen_ai_request_model, codexlb_request_kind) (increase(gen_ai_client_time_to_first_token_seconds_count{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_family=~"$family", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_service_tier_requested!~"priority"}[$__range])), 1)) - (sum by (gen_ai_request_model, codexlb_request_kind) (increase(gen_ai_client_time_to_first_token_seconds_sum{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_family=~"$family", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_service_tier_requested="priority"}[$__range])) / clamp_min(sum by (gen_ai_request_model, codexlb_request_kind) (increase(gen_ai_client_time_to_first_token_seconds_count{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_family=~"$family", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_service_tier_requested="priority"}[$__range])), 1))) / clamp_min((sum by (gen_ai_request_model, codexlb_request_kind) (increase(gen_ai_client_time_to_first_token_seconds_sum{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_family=~"$family", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_service_tier_requested!~"priority"}[$__range])) / clamp_min(sum by (gen_ai_request_model, codexlb_request_kind) (increase(gen_ai_client_time_to_first_token_seconds_count{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_family=~"$family", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_service_tier_requested!~"priority"}[$__range])), 1)), 0.001)) and on (gen_ai_request_model, codexlb_request_kind) (sum by (gen_ai_request_model, codexlb_request_kind) (increase(gen_ai_client_time_to_first_token_seconds_count{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_family=~"$family", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_service_tier_requested="priority"}[$__range])) > 0) and on (gen_ai_request_model, codexlb_request_kind) (sum by (gen_ai_request_model, codexlb_request_kind) (increase(gen_ai_client_time_to_first_token_seconds_count{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_family=~"$family", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_service_tier_requested!~"priority"}[$__range])) > 0)

spec.title: Turn-duration sample sizes by model
spec.description: The exact denominator for the end-to-end comparison below. Blank is normal and priority is fast; only real user-visible turns enter this histogram.

spec.title: Fast end-to-end turn improvement by model
spec.description: Mean user-visible turn-duration improvement within each model. Positive is faster. Turn duration only records real turns, so request kind is not a dimension here.

spec.expr: (100 * ((sum by (gen_ai_request_model) (increase(codexlb_turn_duration_seconds_sum{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_family=~"$family", codexlb_service_tier_requested!~"priority"}[$__range])) / clamp_min(sum by (gen_ai_request_model) (increase(codexlb_turn_duration_seconds_count{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_family=~"$family", codexlb_service_tier_requested!~"priority"}[$__range])), 1)) - (sum by (gen_ai_request_model) (increase(codexlb_turn_duration_seconds_sum{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_family=~"$family", codexlb_service_tier_requested="priority"}[$__range])) / clamp_min(sum by (gen_ai_request_model) (increase(codexlb_turn_duration_seconds_count{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_family=~"$family", codexlb_service_tier_requested="priority"}[$__range])), 1))) / clamp_min((sum by (gen_ai_request_model) (increase(codexlb_turn_duration_seconds_sum{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_family=~"$family", codexlb_service_tier_requested!~"priority"}[$__range])) / clamp_min(sum by (gen_ai_request_model) (increase(codexlb_turn_duration_seconds_count{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_family=~"$family", codexlb_service_tier_requested!~"priority"}[$__range])), 1)), 0.001)) and on (gen_ai_request_model) (sum by (gen_ai_request_model) (increase(codexlb_turn_duration_seconds_count{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_family=~"$family", codexlb_service_tier_requested="priority"}[$__range])) > 0) and on (gen_ai_request_model) (sum by (gen_ai_request_model) (increase(codexlb_turn_duration_seconds_count{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_family=~"$family", codexlb_service_tier_requested!~"priority"}[$__range])) > 0)

options.content:
The critical path decomposes one response into **pre-inference → engine wall → sampling and stream**,
plus whatever is left over. Each stage is a histogram in its own right, so a slow turn can be attributed
rather than guessed at. `critical_path_coverage` on the stage metrics tells you whether the stages
actually account for the whole response - when it says partial, the decomposition is missing a piece and
the leftovers land in *other*.

The `engine_*` family is the upstream provider's own timing, reported back in the frames: **service**
timings are what the serving layer measured, **iapi** timings are what the inner inference API measured.
`service_minus_iapi_tbt` is the gap between them - queueing and transport that belongs to neither model.

The `responses_excl_*` family is the same response measured with different things subtracted, so you can
isolate what a stage costs by comparing two of them rather than trusting a single attribution.

spec.title: Critical path stages (p95)
spec.description: Stacked p95 by stage. Stacking quantiles is not arithmetically exact - p95s do not sum - but it is the fastest way to see WHICH stage moved, which is the question this panel exists to answer. Use the mean panel below when you need the sum to be honest.

spec.title: Critical path stages (mean, additive)
spec.description: Means DO sum, so this stack is a true decomposition. Split by critical_path_coverage so a partial attribution cannot masquerade as a complete one.

spec.title: Engine wall by family
spec.description: Time the upstream engine was working, as it reported it. The low-level histogram retains family for probe exclusion but omits model to stay within the measured active-series budget; use operation duration for model cohorts.

spec.title: Service vs IAPI inference
spec.description: Two measurements of the same inference from different layers. A widening gap is overhead between them, not a slower model.

spec.title: Service vs IAPI sampling
spec.description: Same pairing for the sampling phase - generating tokens once the prompt is processed.

spec.title: Time between tokens
spec.description: TBT is what streaming feels like. The service-minus-iapi gap is transport and queueing between the two layers - if that is what is large, the model is not the problem.

spec.title: Time to first token (gen_ai semconv)
spec.description: TTFT dominates perceived responsiveness far more than total duration does.

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, gen_ai_request_model) (rate(gen_ai_client_time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_family=~"$family", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, gen_ai_request_model) (rate(gen_ai_client_time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_family=~"$family", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, gen_ai_request_model) (rate(gen_ai_client_time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_family=~"$family", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

spec.title: Time to first token by REQUESTED service tier
spec.description: Whether priority processing is worth having. Grouped by what the client ASKED for, because what the server reports having served is not a usable answer: across every response after the 2026-08-08 cutover the request said priority and the response said default, never once priority. So this panel, and the mean below, are the measurement - the served label is not. The series with no tier is the pre-cutover baseline, absent rather than empty; once every request asks for a tier it stops advancing and the comparison becomes historical rather than live.

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, codexlb_service_tier_requested) (rate(gen_ai_client_time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_family=~"$family", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, codexlb_service_tier_requested) (rate(gen_ai_client_time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_family=~"$family", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, codexlb_service_tier_requested) (rate(gen_ai_client_time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_family=~"$family", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

spec.title: Turn duration mean by requested service tier
spec.description: The mean, not a quantile, and end-to-end rather than to-first-token: a tier change should move the whole distribution, and comparing two p95s across a changeover conflates the shift with whatever else moved in the window. Read it alongside the TTFT panel above - TTFT is where a queueing change shows up first and largest.

spec.expr: sum by (codexlb_service_tier_requested) (rate(codexlb_turn_duration_seconds_sum{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_family=~"$family"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum by (codexlb_service_tier_requested) (rate(codexlb_turn_duration_seconds_count{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_family=~"$family"}[$__rate_interval])), 0.001)

spec.title: Response duration, with stages excluded
spec.description: The same response with different components subtracted. Differences between these lines ARE the components - this is how you attribute latency without trusting a single computed breakdown.

spec.title: gen_ai client operation duration (by status)
spec.description: The OTel GenAI standard latency histogram, split by outcome. Errors that are FAST and errors that are SLOW are different failures.

spec.title: Engine wall heatmap
spec.description: The distribution rather than its summary. Bimodality - two bands - means two populations of request, which a p95 line hides completely. A single narrow vertical band is the backlog-replay artifact described on the Overview tab, not a real burst: every bucket was filled during one catch-up pass.

spec.title: Client tool pause
spec.description: Time the model spent waiting on a CLIENT-side tool - the harness, not the provider. Expected empty on this capture. When it is not empty, this is latency you own and can actually fix.

spec.title: Tool call rate by tool
spec.description: Which tools the agent actually reaches for.

spec.title: Tool calls in range
spec.description: Same data ranked. The long tail is usually more interesting than the head.

spec.title: Tool calls per operation
spec.description: How many tools one response invokes. A rising p99 is an agent looping - it costs tokens and latency without necessarily failing, so nothing else alerts.

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, gen_ai_request_model) (rate(gen_ai_client_tool_calls_per_operation_count_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, gen_ai_request_model) (rate(gen_ai_client_tool_calls_per_operation_count_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, gen_ai_request_model) (rate(gen_ai_client_tool_calls_per_operation_count_bucket{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind"}[$__rate_interval])))

spec.title: Tool call records
spec.description: Individual tool invocations with arguments, bounded at 16KB per call. Truncation is marked inline with the original length.

spec.title: Tool output records
spec.description: What came back. Paired with the call above by turn and thread id.

spec.title: Subagent activity
spec.description: Turns attributable to a subagent rather than the top-level thread. Only the instructions record carries subagent lineage, which is why this is derived from turns rather than counted directly.

spec.expr: sum by (codexlb_subagent_kind) (increase(codexlb_turns_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family"}[$__range]))

spec.title: Instructions records (agent lineage)
spec.description: The only record carrying parent_thread_id, parent_turn_id, forked_from_thread_id and subagent_kind - the agent tree lives here. instructions_hash lets you tell a prompt change from a prompt reuse.

spec.title: Agent messages
spec.description: What the agent said, as opposed to what it did.

spec.title: Agent-message topology
spec.description: Author to recipient edges from agent-message records. This is the message topology rather than an inferred tree.

spec.title: Parent and child threads
spec.description: Parent and child thread pairs from the instruction record that establishes agent lineage.

spec.title: Primary window utilisation
spec.description: Percent of the account's primary rate-limit window consumed. This is reported BY the provider in the frames, not inferred here.

spec.title: Secondary window utilisation
spec.description: The independently reported secondary limit window. Its plan type is retained so unlike accounts are never averaged together.

spec.title: Per-model window utilisation
spec.description: Some models carry their own window. This one can be exhausted while the primary window above still looks healthy - that mismatch is exactly the case worth watching.

spec.title: Time until window reset
spec.description: Sawtooth is healthy - it should fall to zero and jump back. A flat line means the value has stopped being refreshed and everything above it is stale.

spec.title: Current utilisation
spec.description: At-a-glance headroom per account.

spec.title: Traffic by plan type and service tier
spec.description: Plan governs the limits; tier governs the queue. Both change what a given latency number means.

spec.expr: sum by (codexlb_plan_type, codexlb_service_tier) (increase(codexlb_responses_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family"}[$__range]))

spec.title: Requested vs served service tier
spec.description: What was asked for against what the platform says it served. These do NOT agree and are not expected to: measured over the 332 responses following the 2026-08-08 priority cutover, every request asked priority and every response reported default (321) or auto (9). Whether that is the platform declining to serve priority or simply not reporting it is not answerable from the capture, so both sides are carried and this panel shows the disagreement rather than resolving it. The latency tab is where the question of whether it MATTERS gets answered.

spec.expr: sum by (codexlb_service_tier_requested, codexlb_service_tier) (increase(codexlb_responses_total{job="codexlb2otel", gen_ai_request_model=~"$model", codexlb_account_id=~"$account", codexlb_request_kind=~"$kind", codexlb_family=~"$family"}[$__range]))

spec.title: Engine calls by account
spec.description: Upstream invocations attributed to each account - the thing the rate limits above are actually counting.

spec.title: Error rate by type and code
spec.description: Errors carried in the archive - the provider's and the harness's, not this exporter's. For the exporter's own health use the Pipeline tab.

spec.title: Errors by model and status
spec.description: Errors concentrated on one model are a different problem from errors spread across all of them.

spec.title: Transport events
spec.description: WebSocket-level events - connection open, close, error - split by close code. A close-code storm here explains latency and error spikes that look inexplicable at the response layer.

spec.title: Safety buffering events
spec.description: The provider held the stream back for a safety check. Directly visible to the user as a stall, and invisible in every latency histogram that measures the engine rather than the stream.

spec.title: Error records
spec.description: Full error records including error_message and error_code, with the thread and turn ids needed to find what the user was doing at the time.

spec.title: Transport records
spec.description: Individual transport frames with transport_event and frame_type.

options.content:
Nine record types reach Loki: **turn, message, agent_message, prompt, instructions, tool_call, tool_output, error, transport**. Only three fields are stream
**labels** (`service_name`, `codexlb_family`, `codexlb_record_type`) - everything else rides as
**structured metadata**, which is queryable without opening a new stream per value. That split is the
entire reason this pipeline pushes to Loki natively instead of using OTLP logs.

Lines older than `loki.max_line_age` (3h) are dropped **here**, deliberately, rather than being handed
to Loki to discard silently behind a 204. Catching up on a backlog therefore produces a
`too_old` rejection count on the Pipeline tab and a gap here - that is the design working, not a fault.

spec.title: Record volume by type
spec.description: All nine types stacked. Ratios between them are stable in normal operation, so a change in shape is a change in how the agent is being used.

spec.title: Record volume by family
spec.description: websocket vs unknown. A rising unknown share means frames are arriving in a shape the classifier does not recognise - worth investigating before it becomes a silent gap.

spec.title: User prompts
spec.description: What was actually asked. Carries the same thread/session/window metadata as everything else, so any line here pivots straight into the matching turn.

spec.title: Messages
spec.description: Conversation messages carrying full token accounting per line.

spec.title: All records, live
spec.description: Everything, filtered by the tab variables. The catch-all view for when you do not yet know which record type holds the answer.

spec.title: Search all record content
spec.description: Case-insensitive regex over line content, driven by the $search variable at the top. Leave it as . to match everything.

spec.title: Lookup by request, response, or thread ID
spec.description: Exact lookup across every record kind by request_id, response_id, or thread_id. Leave $id blank until an identifier is pasted.

spec.expr: {service_name="codexlb2otel", codexlb_record_type=~"$record_type"} | json request_id="request_id", response_id="response_id", thread_id="thread_id" | (request_id!="" and request_id="$id") or (response_id!="" and response_id="$id") or (thread_id!="" and thread_id="$id")

options.content:
One trace per **logical turn**. The root span is `turn`; under it sit the critical-path
children - `critical_path.pre_inference`, `critical_path.engine_wall`,
`critical_path.sampling_and_stream`, `critical_path.client_tool_pause` and `critical_path.other` - plus a
`generateText`/`streamText <model>` span per model call and an
`execute_tool <tool>` or `invoke_agent <agent>` span per tool
invocation. Span names follow the OTel GenAI convention of `<operation> <target>`, so the model and
tool name are in the span name as well as in attributes.

The same decomposition appears as histograms on the **Latency** tab. Use these when you need one
specific slow turn; use the histograms when you need the shape across all of them.

spec.title: Slowest turns
spec.description: Root spans over 30 seconds. Click a trace id to open the waterfall and see which critical-path child owns the time.

spec.title: Recent turns
spec.description: Every logical turn as a trace, newest first.

spec.title: Tool execution spans
spec.description: One span per tool call, carrying the bounded arguments. The 16KB bound is applied at a rune boundary, so a truncated argument is still valid UTF-8.

spec.title: Agent invocation spans
spec.description: Spawn-agent calls as their own GenAI operation, including the child agent name and bounded task metadata.

spec.title: Model call spans
spec.description: The inference spans. Span name is `<operation> <model>`, so the model is greppable without opening the span, and the operation says whether the response streamed. Named generateText/streamText rather than the GenAI convention's `chat` because that is the vocabulary Grafana agent observability recognises - see attr's GenAIOperationGenerateText (#32).

spec.title: Critical path spans
spec.description: The stage spans on their own, for when you want to compare one stage across many turns rather than all stages within one turn.

spec.title: Errored turns
spec.description: Traces whose root span carries error status. Empty is the expected state.

spec.title: This tab is about the exporter, not the agent

options.content:
Everything on the other tabs describes codex-lb's traffic. This tab describes **codexlb2otel itself** -
whether it is keeping up, whether it is losing data, and whether its sinks are accepting what it sends.

**Ingest lag is the metric that catches every other failure first.** It is the only wall-clock
subtraction in the pipeline; all other timing is measured against the archive's own clock so that
catching up on a backlog does not look like an outage.

One trap worth stating: `files_reclaimed` staying flat while retention is enabled means deletion is
**failing**, not that nothing was due - a read-only archive mount returns EROFS on every attempt.

spec.title: Ingest lag
spec.description: Sustained growth means the tailer is falling behind the writer. Healthy is around the poll interval.

spec.title: Read throughput
spec.description: Compressed archive bytes consumed per second. Spikes on startup as the backlog is worked through, then settles to the write rate.

spec.title: Decode pipeline
spec.description: The three stages of reduction. Lines far exceeding turns is normal - many frames reduce to one turn.

spec.title: Partial member reads
spec.description: A gzip member cut off mid-write at the tail of the file. This is the NORMAL steady state of tailing a file being appended to, and a healthy rate here is the signal that ingestion is keeping up. Deliberately never conflated with decode errors below.

spec.title: Data faults
spec.description: A complete-but-corrupt gzip member, or a line that would not parse. Unlike partial reads above, these are real faults: counted, dropped, and the checkpoint moves past them so one bad byte cannot wedge the pipeline.

spec.title: Archive files
spec.description: Watched should track the retention window. Replacements count a file recreated at the same name as different content - real behaviour, caught by fingerprinting the head rather than trusting the path.

spec.title: Current file offset
spec.description: How far into the live archive file the checkpoint has advanced. Sawtooth as each hour's file rolls over.

spec.title: Reducer state
spec.description: Open responses growing without bound means completion frames are not arriving. Persisted series and threads are never pruned by design, so slow growth is expected and fast growth is not. Evictions are in-flight responses given up on - measured against the archive's watermark, not the wall clock, so a backlog does not evict everything on the first pass.

spec.title: Sink backlog
spec.description: Lines buffered and not yet pushed, per sink. Should hover near zero and return to it.

spec.title: Sink rejections (rate)
spec.description: Deliveries refused, BY REASON - the reason matters far more than the count. too_old is the Loki max_line_age guard dropping backlog locally rather than letting Loki discard it behind a 204, and is expected while catching up. unauthorized or bad_request is a config fault that will NOT fix itself and holds the checkpoint until someone intervenes.

spec.title: Sink rejections in range
spec.description: The rate panel goes flat once rejections stop. This panel counts only rejections that occurred inside the selected range and handles process counter resets.

spec.title: Enrichment lookups by result
spec.description: Postgres enrichment outcomes: cache_hit, db_hit, miss, error, or disabled.

spec.title: Enrichment cache hit rate
spec.description: Cache hits as a share of every enrichment attempt. Disabled enrichment is included so a configuration change remains visible.

spec.title: Enrichment lookup latency
spec.description: Database-attempt lookup latency. Cache hits and disabled enrichment deliberately have no synthetic zero observation.

spec.title: Enrichment cache entries
spec.description: Response rows currently held by the enrichment LRU.

spec.title: Breaking archive drift findings
spec.description: Current breaking differences from the embedded archive baseline.

spec.title: Exporter log stream
spec.description: codexlb2otel's OWN stdout, collected by the docker integration - a different stream from the conversation records it pushes. This is where a flush failure or a config fault says so in words.
